Guillermo's own take for Sat, Nov 7 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Outflow day in Howe Sound. Environment Canada has a gale warning, northerly 25 to 35 this morning. At 5am Pam Rocks read only N 8 gusting 15, so it's behind the page for now, but the English Bay buoy already has NNE 15 and Pemberton is 2 hPa above Vancouver.

My pick is Porteau from 9am to 1pm, NNE 26 to 28 on the page, with swell up to about 3.5ft around midday. The tide drops to 9.8ft near 11am, then floods. Go if Pam Rocks reads 22+ from the north by 9am.

Late afternoon, Howe Sound may flip to a southerly inflow.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 04:00 AM PCT 07 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Sunday. Gale warning in effect. Wind northerly outflow 10 to 15 knots increasing to northerly outflow 15 to 25 early this morning and to northerly outflow 25 to 35 late this morning. Wind becoming southerly inflow 25 to 35 early this evening then diminishing to southerly inflow 15 to 25 Sunday morning. Wind diminishing to southerly inflow 10 to 15 Sunday evening.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 04:00 AM PCT 07 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Today Tonight and Sunday. Gale warning in effect. Wind east 5 to 15 knots increasing to east 15 to 20 this morning and to southeast 20 to 30 this afternoon. Wind diminishing to southwest 20 Sunday morning and to southwest 10 to 15 Sunday afternoon. Wind diminishing to light Sunday evening.
